scope: Exactly one original short AQA 7405 first-school-mock Chemistry 3.1.10 Kp-specific catalyst explanation; supplement only, not a full Kp coverage sign-off.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does adding a catalyst leave Kp unchanged at constant temperature?
cards.back: It speeds both forward and reverse reactions without changing the equilibrium position or Kp.
accept: A catalyst increases the rates of both forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium composition and Kp remain unchanged.
It only makes equilibrium reached faster, without shifting equilibrium or changing the equilibrium constant.
It affects how quickly equilibrium is attained, not the equilibrium position or Kp at fixed temperature.
reject: The catalyst increases Kp by speeding up the forward reaction more than the reverse.
Catalysts shift equilibrium towards products and raise Kp.
A catalyst lowers Kp by changing the equilibrium partial pressures.
